discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitaet Muenchen, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Zoller and co-workers predicted in 1998 that ultracold bosons in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model, turning atoms in light into a programmable model of strongly correlated matter. In 2002 Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid to Mott insulator quantum phase transition, the first clean realization of a many-body quantum phase transition in a synthetic system. Their work launched the field of analog quantum simulation. Bloch and Greiner later developed quantum gas microscopes with single-atom, single-site resolution, which made it possible to image antiferromagnetic correlations in Fermi-Hubbard systems, string order and many-body localization, while Zoller's theory programme shaped lattice gauge theories and topological models. Together they turned Feynman's idea of quantum simulation into an experimental science. It now addresses open questions in condensed-matter physics and underpins today's neutral-atom quantum computers.
